articles.title: Manchester United's famous loss to Southend United 20 years on
articles.summary: Southend United's heroes remember their famous victory against Manchester United 20 years on.
articles.body:
Twenty years ago, Southend United sent shockwaves through English football as they dumped Manchester United out of the Carling Cup.

A stunning 30-yard free-kick from Freddy Eastwood clinched victory over Sir Alex Ferguson's star-studded side featuring Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney, who were top of the Premier League.

It sparked elation both in the stands and on the pitch at Roots Hall as the struggling Shrimpers, who were bottom of the Championship, progressed to the quarter-finals.

Those involved in Southend's fairytale cup run have relived the club's finest hour with BBC Essex in a four-part podcast .

It was billed as an irresistible David v Goliath match-up: Lowly Southend against the world famous Manchester United in the fourth round of the cup.

Sir Alex made nine changes but still fielded 10 internationals in an attempt to avoid slipping up, with 11,532 fans cramming into Roots Hall to see a potential upset.

Darren Fletcher, Alan Smith and Gabriel Heinze were among the stars to play alongside Ronaldo and Rooney in what was a £58.75m line-up.

"We saw the teamsheet and you do fear the worst," admits Steve Tilson, who was Southend manager on the night.

Goalkeeper Darryl Flahavan recalls first learning of the Red Devils' starting 11 over the stadium's loudspeaker.

"I always remember my goalkeeping coach at the time, Lee Turner, coming up to me and just whispering in my ear, 'I think you're going to be busy tonight, mate'," he says.

Yet despite the odds stacked in their favour, Jon Champion, who commentated on the game, recalls Sir Alex's men looking uncomfortable at the old-school Roots Hall.

"I remember looking at some of them - who'd clearly never seen anything quite like this before in their football careers - and they did look like fish out of water," he says.

Buoyed by an electric atmosphere near the seaside, the side with nothing to lose made a fierce start.

When Jamal Campbell-Ryce was fouled 30 yards from goal in the 27th minute, history was about to be made.

Boyhood United fan Freddy Eastwood had twice before trialled for the Red Devils. He stood over the free-kick with Steven Hammell.

"I said to Stevie just before I hit the ball, 'No, I'm taking it because I'm going to score'," Eastwood reminisces.

Southend's top-scorer arrowed the ball past the Manchester United wall and into the top corner.

"There was just an explosion of noise as the net rippled," Champion says.

"It was a dawning realisation that a very special moment was unfolding."

For Tilson, it began an agonising wait for the full-time whistle: "You look at your watch and you think, 'It's a long time to go. Are we going to be able to hold on?'."

United responded with force, but heroics from Flahavan to twice deny Ronaldo - who went on to be crowned the world's best footballer five times - helped to keep the Old Trafford side at bay.

"I knew it was going to be a big night for me and a night I wanted to do myself justice," Flahavan says.

Eastwood adds: "Ronaldo was everywhere, he was shooting from everywhere – they just didn't get the goal."

"The longer the game goes on and you get down to the last five minutes, you hope and pray you can pull it off," says Tilson.

Referee Uriah Rennie's final whistle prompted scenes of jubilation inside Roots Hall as the home side won 1-0 .

Among the overjoyed fans was legendary singer Alison Moyet, who, such was the high demand, had called in a favour from Tilson for a ticket after he recently watched her perform.

The Southend Echo reported selling a record-breaking number of newspapers the next day, leading to it being reprinted.

Journalists from the nation's media had all desperately pursued the man at the centre of it all for an interview.

"I was getting chased all over the place, I don't think I even went home that night," Eastwood remembers.

"We had a night out the night after and celebrated it properly, because after the game we just couldn't get out the stadium.

"There were so many fans, everyone was so full of joy."

Southend were to continue wrestling against the Premier League elite, as they drew Tottenham Hotspur at White Hart Lane in the quarter-final.

The establishment-defying Shrimpers took Spurs to extra-time and came within five minutes of a penalty shootout, but for a winning Jermain Defoe goal.

Manchester United, meanwhile, went on to win the Premier League and reach the semi-finals of the Champions League.

Tilson, of course, will never forget what his team did against that great side.

"It wasn't a case of we were hanging on for 90 minutes," he insists.

"We played some good football and I thought we thoroughly deserved the win in the end."

articles.title: Simeone, un tormento para Flick
articles.standfirst: El Cholo es el único que le ha derrotado tres veces en su carrera profesional. No perdía tanto con un entrenador desde sus inicios en la Tercera división alemana
articles.summary: El Cholo es el único que le ha derrotado tres veces en su carrera profesional. No perdía tanto con un entrenador desde sus inicios en la Tercera división alemana
articles.body: Más allá de poder irse al parón liguero de la semana que viene en lo más alto de la clasificación y de convertirse ya en solitario en el entrenador con más victorias en la historia del campeonato (ante el Levante igualó los 344 triunfos de Luis Aragonés habiendo disputado 192 partidos menos), Simeone también está en disposición de confirmarse como el mayor estorbo en la carrera de Hansi Flick. No en vano, si el Atlético vence al Barcelona este domingo, será el único técnico en haber conseguido derrotar al alemán cuatro veces desde que en 1996 comenzara su trayectoria en los banquillos en el Victoria Bammental de la Cuarta división del país germano. De hecho, incluso antes de que el balón eche a rodar en el Metropolitano, El Cholo ya constituye la piedra más molesta en el zapato del azulgrana en su andadura por el fútbol profesional. Aunque verse las caras prácticamente supone una costumbre (tras 12 enfrentamientos, dos al frente del Bayern y diez desde su llegada al Camp Nou, el argentino es el técnico al que más veces se ha medido) y pese a que el balance es favorable al alemán (dos empates y siete triunfos que del mismo modo hacen que sea al que más ha ganado), Simeone ha sido capaz de convertirse en el mayor tormento que se ha encontrado Flick. Especialmente desde que dirige al Barcelona, pues ya en su primer duelo, en el destierro a Montjuic de la temporada 24-25, el Atlético obraría una remontada sobre la bocina (1-2) para coronarse campeón de invierno que a su vez constituía la primera victoria del Cholo en LaLiga en el feudo azulgrana. No obstante, las dos derrotas que representan toda una espina clavada para Flick fueron las de la campaña pasada, el 4-0 en 45 minutos que allanó el terreno al Atlético hacia la final de Copa y, dos meses después, el 0-2 en los cuartos de Champions que tampoco sería capaz de voltear el Barcelona en los compromisos de vuelta por más que en ambas ocasiones se apuntara los triunfos más amargos del técnico alemán. Tres triunfos, en definitiva, que nadie más ha sellado ante el hombre que sale a Liga conquistada desde su llegada a la Ciudad Condal, siendo Luis Enrique (dos victorias y un empate) o Marco Rose (dos victorias y dos derrotas) los más ilustres de entre los que han conseguido que Flick doblara la rodilla más de una vez desde que habita en la élite. Tanto es así, que hay que remontarse a sus inicios en el 'barro' para encontrar técnicos que emulen a Simeone. Ni más ni menos que 21 años hay que remontarse para asistir a un entrenador que volteara al ahora entrenador del Barça hasta en tres ocasiones. Robin Dutt, al frente del Stuttgarter Kickers, completaba en la temporada 2005-06 su trienio venciendo como local al Hoffenheim al que Flick había ascendido a la Regionalliga Sud, la Tercera alemana. También Hermann Gerland, que 15 años más tarde acabaría ejerciendo como su asistente tanto en la selección de Alemania como en el Bayern Munich, le endosaría le endosaría tres derrotas dirigiendo al filial del gigante teutón. Dos campañas antes había sido Hans-Jürgen Boysen, tanto en su etapa en el Schweinfurt 05 como en el Kickers Offenbach, el que doblegaría a Flick por tercera vez. Una bienvenida de lo que supone el mundo de los banquillos que le había dado Gerd Schwickert en los ejercicios 01-02 y 02-03, venciéndole con el Wehen en el que se desenvolvía como mediocentro el hoy realista Pellegrino Matarazzo y posteriormente en las filas del SV 07 Elversberg en la temporada 03-04. Eran otros tiempos, otro fútbol y una sensación olvidada por Flick desde que empezó a hacerse un nombre en el Bayern... hasta que apareció Simeone para revivirla como su pesadilla.

articles.title: El Madrid, de caldera en caldera
articles.standfirst: Tras Atenas, visita Valencia, después de jugar hace menos de dos semanas en el Camp Nou y remontar hace tres en Roma
articles.summary: Tras Atenas, visita Valencia, después de jugar hace menos de dos semanas en el Camp Nou y remontar hace tres en Roma
articles.body: El Real Madrid suma siete victorias consecutivas, de las que cuatro han sido fuera de casa. Partidos casi todos ellos muy duros, definidos al final por un equipo que parece haber recuperado el gen competitivo que ha distinguido históricamente a los equipos del club blanco. La última llegó en Atenas, una de las grandes sucursales de los 'infiernos' del deporte europeo, sea fútbol o baloncesto, principalmente. Grecia es, con Turquía, la cuna de las hinchadas más calientes del Viejo Continente. Cada visita a tierras helenas es un dolor de muelas para cualquier equipo europeo, que sabe que el principal obstáculo puede no estar en el terreno de juego. En este sentido, el partido del miércoles en el AEK Stadium no fue una excepción en cuantro al ambiente, pero sí en relación al resultado. El Madrid sólo había ganado en una de sus ocho visitas a Grecia antes del triunfo, agónico, sellado en el minuto 91 gracias un implacable derechazo de Fede Valverde. El Madrid se sobrepuso a un tremendo ambiente en contra, como hace casi dos semanas ocurrió en Barcelona. El Camp Nou tampoco es un estadio precisamente cómodo para el Madrid, enfrentado a los locales en una rivalidad que trasciende lo deportivo y que admite pocas comparaciones a nivel mundial. De nuevo el triunfo llegó en el último suspiro del partido, gracias a un gol de Mbappé a pase de Camavinga. Este sábado, el Madrid visita otra 'caldera', otro de esos estadios en los que el ambiente pesa. Las gradas casi verticales de Mestalla volverán a poner a prueba el temple de los blancos pese a la baja de Vinicius, que inevitablemente restará algo de tensión a la presencia del Madrid en Valencia. Pero Mestalla no es un campo fácil para los blancos. En las últimas diez temporadas, pese a la pujanza del Madrid (sobre todo en la Champions) y la crisis de identidad del Valencia, el balance es equilibrado: cuatro victorias locales, cuatro visitantes y dos empates. El factor Mestalla tratará de hacerse notar de nuevo este sábado ante el Madrid, que llega con la intención de prolongar su racha, fraguada sobre todo en los nervios de acero mostrado en las victorias como vistante ante Roma, Barça y AEK. Tres situaciones límite, ante hinchadas muy calientes, que el Madrid supo sortear.

articles.title: Santiago Bernabéu, el primer goleador en los Valencia-Madrid
articles.standfirst: La rivalidad nació en Mestalla, el primer día de mayo de 1926
articles.summary: La rivalidad nació en Mestalla, el primer día de mayo de 1926
articles.body: El Real Madrid, salvo que la Copa diga lo contrario, se despide de Mestalla. Por última vez en la Liga, el equipo blanco pisa un estadio en el que ha vivido batallas de alta intensidad. Desde el inicio, porque en el primer partido de Liga en la casa del Valencia, el equipo del murciélago amagó con retirarse del campo a causa del arbitraje. Ese voltaje lo lleva disparado desde hace años. El fichaje de Mijatovic por el Madrid cambió de manera radical la relación entre los dos clubes. Antes del cierre de esta noche en el templo del valencianismo, el Valencia ha recibido al Madrid en 228 ocasiones, contando todo tipo de partidos. La victoria se quedó a orillas del Turia en 63, se fue a Madrid en 118 y los empates fuero 47. El valencianista que más holes ha al Madrid en Mestalla es Mundo Suárez, con 13; en el sentido contrario aparece Raúl (17); Vicente Asensi (28 partidos) es el que más partidos jugó;la mayor victoria del Valencia es el 6-0 de las semifinales de Copa del 9 de junio de 1999; para el Madrid, el 1-7 del 1 - 7 23 de agosto de 1990, en el Trofeo Naranja. Todo empezó el 1 de mayo de 1926. En ese mes, la ciudad de Valencia se volcó como nunca antes en la celebración de la fiesta de la Cruz de Mayo. Numerosas entidades culturales de la ciudad se sumaron a las iniciativas oficiales. Al otro lado, la estrecha vigilancia desplegada en toda España por la dictadura de Primo de Rivera buscaba minimizar las manifestaciones obreras en el Día del Trabajo. En ese contexto festivo, el Valencia invitó al Real Madrid a jugar dos partidos en Mestalla. Inaugurada el 20 de mayo de 1923, la nueva casa valencianista aún no había vivido partidos ante el Madrid. Sí, como antes en Algirós, ante otros equipos de la capital: Racing, Gimnástica y Stadium. La presencia del Madrid en Valencia y en las fiestas de mayo generó una enorme expectación. Las entradas volaron para los dos partidos, que se iban a jugar en solo 24 horas: el 1 y el 2 de mayo. Meses antes, en plenas Navidades, el equipo blanco había viajado a la capital del Turia. Pero para jugar, y perder dos veces, ante el Levante: 3-1 y 1-0 en La Creu. A las seis de la tarde del 1 de mayo de 1926 rodó la pelota por primera vez en Mestalla en un duelo entre Valencia y Real Madrid. Con más suplentes que titulares en los dos equipos, la tarde arrancó vibrante. Los Valencia-Madrid están repletos de acciones que han hecho correr ríos de tinta y alimentado airados debates. Así comenzó el primer duelo en Mestalla. Santiago Bernabéu, delantero centro del Madrid esa tarde, abrió el marcador a los tres minutos. Los jugadores del Valencia reclamaron fuera de juego cuando Monjardín lanzó en carrera a Del Campo, asistente de Bernabéu. En la grada pareció claro, pero el árbitro, el valenciano José Monterde Seguí, dio validez al tanto. A pesar de ese mal arranque, el Valencia fue el triunfador de una tarde en la que entusiasmó a su gente con su juego y su brío. Del 0-1 nada más empezar se pasó al 3-1 al descanso. Empató Quesada, le dio ventaja Roca, que marró un penalti a los 34 minutos pero aprovechó el rechazo de Martínez para marcar, y Arróniz puso el 3-1. Superior en cada parte del campo, el cuarto gol valencianista llegó a la hora de juego con un tanto espléndido de José Llago II. La tarde iba camino de una gran goleada. Al margen de los cuatro goles, el Madrid daba síntomas de agotamiento. Pero el equipo de la capital sacó fuerzas de flaqueza. Un disparo soberbio de Bernabéu valió para el 4-2. Y, en el último minuto, Monjardín dio emoción con el tercer gol madridista, pero no hubo tiempo para más. Con una cerrada ovación premió el numeroso público a los dos equipos por el brillante espectáculo ofrecido. Y se frotaba las manos porque el partido se repetía a las cinco y media de la tarde del día siguiente. Sin embargo... Con las gradas de Mestalla abarrotadas, a la hora fijada dio el pitido inicial Rafael Piquer. El cielo amenazaba. Y antes de la media hora de partido se abrió para descargar una monumental tromba de agua. Se detuvo el juego y el temporal pareció menguar. Pero, cuando los dos equipos acordaron volver a jugar, se recrudeció de tal manera que fue imposible continuar. A finales de agosto de 1926, toda España sufrió un terrible temporal que provocó centenares de muertos. El Madrid regresó a Mestalla el 29 de abril de 1928. Esta vez para jugar un partido oficial: la vuelta de los cuartos de final de Copa. Ganó el Valencia por 2-1 para meterse en semifinales después del empate a uno del día 15 en Chamartín.

articles.title: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid are set to take on Valencia at Mestalla later today as they look to continue their excellent form ahead of the international break.The last seven...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are set to take on Valencia at Mestalla later today as they look to continue their excellent form ahead of the international break.

The last seven games have been a breeze for Los Blancos , with Jose Mourinho's side putting in excellent performances.

This has been crucial in strengthening belief in the project that the Portuguese manager is building at the Santiago Bernabeu .

Mourinho's men will be looking to make it eight in a row before the November international break.

Standing in their way is Javier Aguirre, an experienced manager who has taken over in an attempt to save Valencia's sinking ship.

According to Diario AS , the Mexican manager has faced Los Blancos 27 times in his career, securing just four victories.

He has suffered 16 defeats and managed seven draws, giving him a win percentage of just 14.8%.

Javier Aguirre has a lot of experience managing on the touchline. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images)

Interestingly, two of his four victories came during his time as Osasuna manager. The first came in February 2003, when he secured a 1-0 victory over Madrid.

Vicente del Bosque was Los Blancos ' manager at the time. Aguirre followed that up with a 3-0 victory over Madrid in April 2004.

His third triumph came in April 2011, when Real Zaragoza secured a stunning 3-2 victory over Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid at the Bernabeu .

His most recent victory came in 2023, when Mallorca defeated Carlo Ancelotti's side 1-0.

Aguirre is an experienced manager who knows every trick in the book, and he can make life very uncomfortable for Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid.

The Mexican is already said to be preparing with a back five ahead of the game in an attempt to stop Los Blancos ' attack.

Mourinho will hope to make it eight defeats in a row against Valencia. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Aguirre has got the better of Mourinho on occasion, but the two sides could hardly be in more contrasting positions heading into this encounter.

Real Madrid are the most in-form team in Europe, while Valencia sit 19th, battling relegation and desperately hoping for a turnaround.

Los Blancos are playing their fourth consecutive away match and will hope to emerge victorious against Los Che .

It promises to be an exciting battle between two experienced managers, and it remains to be seen whether Mourinho can add another defeat to Aguirre's poor record tonight.

articles.title: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms
articles.summary: The link between local music and Manchester City fans has always been present, most obviously through Britpop legends Oasis, and now a new kit release has br...
articles.body:
The link between local music and Manchester City fans has always been present, most obviously through Britpop legends Oasis, and now a new kit release has brought a different Greater Manchester artist to the doorstep.

Stockport indie outfit Blossoms, who are also lifelong supporters of the club, have teamed up with the Blues to release a limited run of charity shirts celebrating four decades of local outreach across the region.

With City in the Community celebrating its 40th anniversary during the ongoing 2026/27 season, main club sponsor Etihad Airways has stepped aside from their front-of-shirt position to make way for the band's logo on the hugely popular 2024/25 away kit.

As announced on the club's official website this week, the special charity drop puts a new spin on a modern favourite.

While Blossoms take over the main shirt sponsor space across the chest, the Etihad Airways logo shifts onto the sleeve, sitting alongside a dedicated CITC logo printed inside the neck to mark the anniversary.

Blossoms celebrated their fifth Official UK Number One album with 'Songs From The Wedding Cake' last month and are about to head out on a major arena tour across the country.

Anyone hoping to pick up a shirt will have to act fast, with initial sizes dropping exclusively at the new flagship CityStore before further batches go on sale around their upcoming homecoming shows at Manchester's Co-op Live in November and December.

Four decades of supporting Greater Manchester

Founded back in 1986, City in the Community has spent 40 years delivering health, education, and social inclusion initiatives to youth across Greater Manchester, and all profits from the special shirt drop will go straight to the charity to help sustain its daily programmes and expand its reach throughout the local area.

To make an even bigger impact across the campaign, Manchester City will match every fan donation made to the foundation on a pound-for-pound basis until the end of May, up to a total of £200,000.

As Enzo Maresca's side keep pushing for results on the pitch, this joint effort between local musicians, sponsors, and Manchester City gives fans another brilliant reason to get behind the community off it.

On the pitch, Enzo Maresca and his players will be wanting to maintain the winning performance they showed in the UEFA Champions League and a 2-3 victory at RB Leipzig , and taking those levels into their next Premier League clash away to Nottingham Forest .

articles.title: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Barcelona could also turn to Gavi for Sunday’s LaLiga meeting with Atletico Madrid, although Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong remain stronger candidates to re...
articles.body:
Barcelona could also turn to Gavi for Sunday's LaLiga meeting with Atletico Madrid, although Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong remain stronger candidates to replace the injured Rodri, reports Mundo Deportivo

For now, manager Hansi Flick has several midfield alternatives available for this clash, with the decision likely to depend on multiple factors, including experience and form.

This situation arrives as Rodri has been ruled out after medical tests confirmed a minor injury to his right hamstring.

Barcelona announced on November 4 that the midfielder would miss the crucial La Liga fixture, leaving Flick with an important selection decision ahead of the trip to the Metropolitano.

Gavi's inclusion in the discussion is particularly interesting given his experience in high-pressure matches and his ability to adapt to different midfield roles.

However, it is crucial to note that the 22-year-old should not be considered the leading candidate at this stage.

Bernal and De Jong lead Barcelona's midfield options

Marc Bernal has solid grounds to replace Rodri. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The academy graduate has already demonstrated his suitability for the role, having started against Elche, Athletic Club, Rayo Vallecano and Paris Saint-Germain this season.

Furthermore, De Jong is another possibility after recovering from his injury problems.

The Dutchman returned during the Clasico and subsequently started against Alaves, although he was a substitute against Aston Villa. His experience and ability to control possession offer Flick a different profile from Bernal.

Gavi's experience in decisive matches gives Flick a strong option

Gavi's case is built on his performances during the closing stages of Barcelona's previous campaign.

After recovering from his serious knee injury, the midfielder became an important option for Flick in several demanding fixtures, demonstrating that he could be trusted when the stakes were high.

Gavi will bring a different profile than Frenkie de Jong and Bernal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

He featured in the Catalan derby against Espanyol, where he operated as a left winger, before starting in tricky away encounters against Osasuna and Getafe.

He also played as a central midfielder in El Clasico against Real Madrid, the match in which Barcelona mathematically secured the La Liga title.

Those appearances showed Gavi's tactical flexibility and competitive intensity.

His ability to press aggressively, recover possession, and support attacking transitions gives Flick a different midfield profile from both Bernal and De Jong.

As stated before, the decision will depend on the type of performance Flick expects against Atletico.

Bernal offers the most natural replacement for Rodri, while De Jong brings greater experience in controlling possession. Gavi, on the other hand, could provide intensity and tactical flexibility in a physically demanding contest.

articles.title: UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction: Can the Bruins Stay Hot?
articles.summary: It won't be that cold in Minneapolis, but the weather isn't the only factor when UCLA takes on the Gophers. Here's our prediction and game preview.
articles.body:
Now it becomes real for UCLA. The Bruins were No. 8 in the first round of College Football Playoff rankings, which doesn't matter. If they end up 10-2, as a Big Ten team, they're a mortal lock to get into the CFP. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game.

UCLA gets Illinois in the Rose Bowl next, then has to travel to Michigan, and finishes up down the road at USC.

Minnesota goes to Penn State next week, hosts Northwestern, and close with the Paul Bunyan Axe game at Wisconsin.

The two programs have only faced each other four times, with Minnesota winning the last meeting 21-17 in 2024. The Gophers are 3-1, starting with a 21-3 win in the 19162 Rose Bowl.

Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10

Run, run, and keep running. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However …

UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too.

UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines

The whole Big Noon Kickoff aspect to this is a problem for UCLA. The Bruins have to be ready to rumble at 9:00 am Los Angeles time. And then there's the other issue. When the ball gets kicked off in Minneapolis, it will be around 71 degrees in LA. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday.

articles.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga set for emotional Athletic Club homecoming at San Mames as Arsenal backup goalkeeper is called up by Basque Country to face Venezuela
articles.summary: Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque...
articles.body:
Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque Country representative team. The shot-stopper has been named in the Euskal Selekzioa squad to take on South American visitors Venezuela during next weekend's international friendly in Bilbao.

Record-breaking keeper returns to Bilbao

Osasuna manager Jagoba Arrasate has included the Ondarroa native as one of the marquee names in his 22-man selection for the clash on Saturday, November 14. Currently serving as understudy to David Raya at Arsenal following previous loan stints with Real Madrid and Bournemouth, Arrizabalaga originally departed Bilbao for Chelsea in 2018. That €80 million move to Stamford Bridge remains the world-record transfer fee ever paid for a goalkeeper.

Joining Arrizabalaga in the squad as players plying their trade outside Spain are Udinese forward Unai Gomez and Bolton Wanderers attacker Gaizka Larrazabal, while Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez provides competition between the posts. Arrasate has once again leaned heavily on a familiar domestic core drawn from Athletic Club, Real Sociedad, Osasuna and Deportivo Alaves.

In defence, Athletic's Dani Vivian, Hugo Rincon and Johaneko Louis-Jean are joined by Sociedad trio Jon Pacheco, Igor Zubeldia and Aihen Munoz alongside Osasuna's Inigo Arguibide and Malaga's Einar Galilea.

Midfield options feature Athletic's Mikel Jauregizar, Sociedad's Benat Turrientes, Alaves pair Pablo Ibanez and Ander Guevara, Osasuna's Asier Osambela and Sevilla's Jon Guridi, while Athletic star Oihan Sancet, Osasuna's Kike Barja and Racing Santander duo Inigo Vicente and Asier Villalibre complete the attack.

Organised by Basque Football Federation president Xabier Goni, the fixture marks the representative team's first appearance since defeating Palestine 3-0 in front of a record 51,396 crowd on November 15 last year via goals from Unai Elgezabal, Gorka Guruzeta and Urko Izeta. Next Saturday's contest carries deep cultural weight as it celebrates the 90th anniversary of the first autonomous Basque Government formed under President Jose Antonio Aguirre in 1936.

Aguirre subsequently established the Euzkadi team in 1937 to tour Europe and the Americas during the Spanish Civil War. Venezuela also holds a special bond with the region after welcoming thousands of Basque political exiles fleeing Francisco Franco's dictatorship.

Hosts defend flawless head-to-head record

Arrrizabalaga will hope to earn rare starting minutes in familiar surroundings next weekend before returning to north London to resume his backup duties under Mikel Arteta after the international break. On the pitch in Bilbao, Euskal Selekzioa will look to preserve their 100 per cent historical record in what will be their fourth meeting against Venezuela. The hosts previously beat the South Americans 4-3 away in San Cristobal in June 2007, 3-1 at the old San Mames in December 2010 and 4-2 at Mendizorrotza in October 2018.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: VfL Bochum vs. Karlsruher SC
articles.summary: The meeting presents an important opportunity for both sides to strengthen their positions in the 2. Bundesliga table as the season progresses. Bochum will b...
articles.body:
The meeting presents an important opportunity for both sides to strengthen their positions in the 2. Bundesliga table as the season progresses. Bochum will be looking to make home advantage count, while Karlsruher SC travel to North Rhine-Westphalia hoping to come away with a positive result.

Bochum head into Sunday's encounter with renewed confidence after ending their difficult run of league form with a 2-1 victory away to Energie Cottbus last weekend.

Uwe Rösler's side had endured a five-game winless run in the league before travelling to Cottbus, but Christian Rasmussen's late winner secured three valuable points and lifted the club to 11th in the standings.

The victory was particularly important given Bochum's struggles in front of goal this season. Having scored just eight times in their opening ten league matches, they currently possess the lowest-scoring attack in the division. However, their recent cup victory over Mainz and the comeback success against Cottbus suggest that Rösler's team are beginning to find some momentum.

Rösler is nevertheless expecting a difficult afternoon against a Karlsruhe side whose intensity and attacking movement could cause problems. Speaking ahead of the fixture, the Bochum coach described Sunday's encounter as a potential 50-50 contest and warned that the visitors are one of the most intense teams in the division.

The German side will need to pay particular attention to Marvin Wanitzek, who Rösler identified as Karlsruhe's standout player, highlighting his ability to find space and influence matches through both open play and set-pieces.

Karlsruher SC travel to Bochum looking to build on an encouraging 2-1 victory over 1. FC Heidenheim, which brought some much-needed stability to their start under new head coach Maximilian Senft.

The Baden-Württemberg outfit had endured a difficult spell before welcoming Heidenheim, having suffered a heavy 6-1 defeat away to Magdeburg immediately after an impressive 4-0 home victory against Darmstadt.

However, goals from Tim Civeja and Marvin Wanitzek secured a deserved victory over the recently-relegated side last weekend, with Wanitzek's superb free-kick proving decisive.

Despite that result, consistency remains a significant concern for Senft. Karlsruhe have collected 11 points from their opening ten league matches, leaving them level with Bochum, although their inferior goal difference places them two positions below Sunday's opponents.

Their away form is another area requiring improvement, with the visitors yet to record an away victory in the league this season, collecting just two points from their four matches on the road.

Senft acknowledged that his team must become more consistent when discussing their recent performances, explaining that the squad are still developing under his new tactical approach.

"We are coming out of the Heidenheim game strengthened, particularly because of the way we performed tactically and mentally," the Austrian coach explained. He also stressed his desire to deliver positive performances more frequently rather than continuing to experience such significant fluctuations.

Karlsruhe will therefore be hoping that last weekend's victory can provide the platform for a more convincing away performance, particularly against a Bochum side who have also struggled to find consistency this season.

Historically, Bochum have enjoyed the better of this fixture, recording 23 victories compared to Karlsruhe's 16 across 64 competitive meetings, with the remaining 25 encounters ending in draws.

However, the more recent record at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion offers encouragement for the visitors. Karlsruhe have avoided defeat on each of their last six visits to Bochum, who have not beaten them at home since a 1-0 victory in May 2014.

Interestingly, 13 of the 24 meetings between the sides in the 2. Bundesliga have ended in draws, highlighting how closely contested this fixture has traditionally been.

The previous meeting came on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign, when Bochum claimed a 2-1 away victory thanks to Moritz-Broni Kwarteng's winning goal.

Bochum will be without several players for Sunday's encounter, with Enis Cokaj, Jean Manuel Mbom and Oliver Olsen having returned to training but not yet being available for selection.

Babis Drakas and Philipp Strompf are also not ready to return, while Berkan Taz missed one training session earlier in the week. However, Rösler confirmed that the remainder of his squad had completed full training.

The Bochum coach also suggested that changes could be made to his attacking partnership, with Philipp Hofmann having played a significant number of minutes recently. Charlie Patiño and Jarne Steuckers are among those pushing for starting opportunities following encouraging substitute appearances.

Karlsruhe, meanwhile, will again be without defensive regulars Marcel Franke and Sebastian Jung, who are both unavailable through injury.

New signing Héliton has completed his first full week of training since the previous international break, although Senft indicated that he is more likely to be considered for a brief appearance rather than a starting role.

Paul Scholl is consequently expected to retain his place in the back three after impressing during the 2-1 victory over Heidenheim, while Tim Civeja will also hope to keep his place following his first goal in the second division.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Heidenheim vs. Hannover 96

articles.body:
The 2. Bundesliga provides an intriguing encounter on the Ostalb, as Heidenheim get set to host Hannover.

Both sides have experienced contrasting fortunes in recent weeks, with Heidenheim struggling to rediscover their early-season form, while Hannover will be looking to build on their first league victory under new head coach Sandro Wagner.

With just four points separating the teams ahead of the 11th matchday, Sunday's meeting presents an important opportunity for both clubs to strengthen their position in the standings.

Heidenheim will be determined to get their promotion challenge back on track after suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Karlsruher SC last weekend.

Frank Schmidt's side appeared to be heading towards a point after Alessandro Vogt equalised late in the contest, only for the hosts to snatch all three points with a stoppage-time winner.

The result extended Heidenheim's winless run in the league to five matches, with their last victory coming against Holstein Kiel back in September.

Despite their recent difficulties, the recently-relegated side remain sixth in the standings with 15 points from their opening ten fixtures. Their home form has also been a positive, with Schmidt's side unbeaten at the Voith-Arena this season, recording three victories and two draws from their five matches.

Sunday's encounter also carries additional significance following Schmidt's announcement earlier this week that he will leave the club at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, bringing an end to his remarkable spell of almost 20 years in charge.

Speaking ahead of the Hannover fixture, Schmidt acknowledged the quality within the opposition ranks but expects an intensely contested encounter.

"Accordingly, Sunday will be a real battle," Schmidt explained, highlighting the importance of intensity, second balls and winning individual duels.

The Heidenheim coach also admitted that his team had been overrun in certain situations during their defeat to Karlsruhe, insisting that his players needed to rediscover their sharpness in training before returning to home action.

With their unbeaten home record on the line, Schmidt will be hoping his side can produce a response and return to winning ways.

Hannover travel to Heidenheim with renewed confidence after finally securing their first league victory under Sandro Wagner last weekend.

The Lower Saxony outfit came from behind to defeat Dynamo Dresden 2-1, with Husseyn Chakroun and Marcel Hartel both scoring within seven second-half minutes to turn the contest around.

The victory was particularly important following a difficult start to Wagner's tenure, which had seen Hannover struggle to translate their attacking potential into consistent results.

Having collected just 11 points from their opening ten league matches, Hannover currently occupy 11th position, leaving them four points behind Sunday's opponents.

Wagner will be encouraged by the character his players demonstrated against Dresden, particularly after falling behind during a difficult opening period. However, their away form remains a significant concern, with their only victory on the road this season coming against Darmstadt. They have lost their other four away fixtures.

Speaking ahead of the trip to Baden-Württemberg, Wagner was full of praise for the opposition, describing Heidenheim as a "top team in the second division".

The Hannover coach also highlighted their distinctive playing style, organisation at set-pieces and attacking presence inside the penalty area, acknowledging that his side face a significant challenge.

Wagner will also be hoping to get more out of Benjamin Källman, who has struggled to replicate the goalscoring form that saw him register 14 goals last season. The Finnish forward has yet to find the net in the current campaign, although his manager remains pleased with his overall contribution.

Nevertheless, last weekend's comeback victory provides Hannover with an opportunity to build some momentum, and another positive result would represent a significant step forward under their new coach.

Heidenheim have historically enjoyed the better of this fixture, winning six of the ten previous meetings between the clubs, compared to Hannover's four victories. Interestingly, none of their ten encounters in the 2. Bundesliga have ended in a draw.

The hosts will also take confidence from their recent record at the Voith-Arena, having won each of their last four home meetings with Hannover.

Their previous encounter came during the 2022/23 campaign, when Heidenheim secured a convincing 3-0 victory away from home, with Tim Kleindienst among the goalscorers.

Hannover's last victory against Heidenheim came in August 2021, when they recorded a 1-0 home success.

Heidenheim have relatively few injury concerns heading into Sunday's fixture, with Luca Kerber the only confirmed absentee.

The midfielder continues to struggle with muscular problems and will not be available for selection. However, Schmidt confirmed during Friday's press conference that the remainder of his squad had been involved in training.

Hannover have a slightly longer injury list, with Lars Gindorf, Benedikt Pichler, and Karl Steinmann all ruled out.

There is more encouraging news regarding Husseyn Chakroun, who suffered a shoulder injury during the Dresden encounter. Wagner confirmed that the attacker would be included in the travelling squad, although a decision on whether he starts or features from the bench will be made closer to kick-off.

Hannover 96 (3-4-2-1): Weinkauf; Ghita, Tomiak, Hugonet; Neubauer, Thordarson, Sahiti, Matsuda; Chakroun, Hartel; Källman.

articles.title: ‘Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm’ As Simon and Garfunkel never sang…
articles.summary: Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled “The Phoney War”, it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Ne...
articles.body:
Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled "The Phoney War" , it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Newcastle United season.

In September I contributed "All Things Bright and Beautiful" , about our promising start to the season.

October's article "Trick or Treat" arrived a little late last weekend. It raised doubts about how things are unfolding after a series of sloppy defeats.

My offering this month? Fire and darkness.

November starts with the dispiriting onset of darkness. As Simon and Garfunkel never sang, "Hello darkness my old friend, soon you'll be here by 5pm."

Darkness aside, there's been more futility than fire from our footballing favourites. Maybe we'll see a spark from Newcastle United in West London on Saturday.

Maybe we'll see two bald men fighting over a comb. An increasingly dull, dreary and desperate attempt to win the coveted prize of being the fourth worst team in the league by the end of the season.

There's always hope , of course, the thing that kills you.

We hope that Fulham will be even more wobbly than us. We hope that we can bag a fourth win of a mercurial season in the capital this weekend. We hope that the likes of Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich, Palace, Fulham will finish below us by the odd point or with a less embarrassing goal difference. We hope that Santa will bring us a little stocking filler in the form of a relegation berth for Man City. If so, we hope that we won't be one of the other two trapdoor teams. We hope that it's going to be alright. We hope Matthias Jaissle will turn it around. We hope that the Newcastle United players will get it. We hope there's something for them to get. We hope for a couple of signings in January. We know all about hope as Newcastle supporters. We know the sorts of things we say in our brighter moments. But November darkness doesn't encourage hope.

There's a beguiling song by an obscure folk singer Dave Goulder, entitled "The January Man". It's partly about the changing seasons, month by month. This month's line is, "The poor November man sees fire and wind and mist and rain and winter air." We can identify with that. So can our current manager, who looked like the poor November man at the end of Monday night's match after shaking hands with the gargoyle Moyes.

If you want a giggle in November's darkness, search up "David Moyes Dunfermline". It should bring up an image of a Soccer Stars/Panini type sticker of a young Davey Moyes in his playing days. Be warned: it belongs on the Halloween clearance shelf. Unsettling. NSFW.

We might giggle but fly old Davey has demonstrated a certain brand of English football to MJ three times these last few months. As my Mam used to say, "that'll learn him a thing or three."

Aggregate score 7-2. Gesundheit, or something that rhymes with it.

Despite the hype of the Premier League being the world's finest, we all know the reality: there's an awful lot of beige football. Much of what is served up is tepid soup prepared by chefs like Moyes, using ingredients from the back of the fridge and the darkest corners of the cupboards. It sustains life but does not bring joy.

Welcome to Richard Masters' soup kitchen. One bit of bread to dunk each, except for the slippery six. They're on the "all you can eat" tariff, butter running down their greasy chins. No soup for them. They're having steak, followed by a selection from the sweet trolley. Coffee. Brandy and cigars.

Here's the recipe for Masters' Beige Football Soup, a tried and trusted staple of the English football diet.

The main ingredients: – a pound of Pulis – five fat Sam fingers – a whiffling of Warnock's whiskers – a measure of Moysie's mustard – a handful of Hughes hoofball – a brace of Bruceballs. Lob in a few streaky rashers and a head of cabbage.

Method: Clag it all into a pan on a low heat until tepid.

Before serving, add the following to taste: – a dash of well-drilled defence – a rasher of rogue refereeing – a pinch of percentages – a layer of long-throw – a jar of "Wee Davey's" jam – a measure of Monday night marinade – a can of barely concealed corruption – a scoop of Stoke soil, ideally harvested on a cold, wet midweek night.

Enough nutritional content and calories to keep you up. Best served lukewarm from a vat of vested interests into leaking, cracked bowls, just enough to accumulate points.

November: the month of fire and darkness. Maybe Matthias Jaissle can kindle fire in the hearts of our lads and us supporters. Maybe there'll be a light in the darkness on Saturday.

articles.title: Non-league's greatest giant-killers eye another scalp
articles.summary: Non-league Altrincham aim to make Notts County number 18 on their list of FA Cup scalps, and breathe new life into their tag of English football's ultimate g...
articles.body:
"I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible."

With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity.

One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions.

Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football.

During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982.

"It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport.

Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions."

Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979.

An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups?

"We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day."

The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. Because despite twice winning what was then the Alliance Premier League, Altrincham were victims of a ballot system that cruelly denied them progression to the Football League - by just a single vote in 1980 - before automatic promotion was introduced a few years later.

Heathcote had left by the time Altrincham pulled off their greatest cup exploit - knocking out first division Birmingham City at St Andrews in 1986 in what remains one of the competition's biggest shocks. They became only the second of four non-league teams to beat top-flight opposition away from home.

Forty years on from that famous night, current manager Neil Gibson is all too aware of the tradition that he now hopes to continue in front of a live BBC TV audience, and a bumper Moss Lane crowd.

Having joined last year to help the club avoid relegation, the Welshman has overseen an impressive start to the current National League campaign, with Altrincham looking like play-off contenders. The dream of a first ever promotion to the EFL is the priority. But Gibson is desperate to build on the recent progress against Notts County.

"It would mean a lot. It's the spirit and essence of this club," he says. "We have a real opportunity. They are a very good team, but it's a game where we feel that we can go and etch our own memories. All the fans remember those cup moments from the past and we want to try and replicate that."

Situated just a few miles from Old Trafford, and in an area of Greater Manchester dominated by fans of United and City, Altrincham has to work hard to maintain its supporter base. But this is a rare moment in the national spotlight for a community club that only turned professional four years ago.

"A lot of our players are good enough to play at a higher level, and it's a chance to showcase themselves and test ourselves against a club that three years ago were in the same league as us," says Gibson, whose squad includes five players that have previously appeared for Notts County.

Gibson has real cup pedigree of his own to draw upon, including against Saturday's opponents. 24 years ago, he played for Conference club Southport as they produced a memorable FA Cup upset over Notts County. He was part of the Tranmere squad that reached the League Cup final in 2000, and he also won the Welsh Cup three times, including twice as a manager.

"Cups have always been very special to me," he says. "We're really excited about it and we're going to give it absolutely everything. But you only remember these days if you come out on the right side of the result."

As for Heathcote, he also managed Altrincham - between 2002 and 2009. And in a remarkable twist of fate, his special connection with the competition has been carried on by his son.

Not content with emulating his father by also playing for Altrincham, Sam Heathcote then helped them to beat League One Barnsley in 2015, the club's most recent cup upset.

And as if that was not enough, having joined local rivals Macclesfield, this year Sam was at the heart of the defence for the National League North side as they stunned then-holders Crystal Palace to produce the greatest shock in FA Cup history, with a staggering 117 places between the sides.

"That far exceeded anything I've done," says Graham, when asked how he explains the Heathcotes' record in the cup across the generations. "I never won in the third round. It's just one of those things!"

Heathcote senior will be at League One side Mansfield on Saturday where he hopes to watch Sam - who works as a teacher in Altrincham - pull off another upset for Macclesfield. But he will also be paying close attention to the action at Moss Lane, and is backing his former club to taste glory once again.

"I'd love to see them get to the third round, so the current generation of Altrincham fans can feel what it's all about," he says. "51 years ago I played at Everton and people still speak about it now. These players have that chance to create such a legacy. Don't just dream about it. Make it happen."

Altrincham's challenge now is to follow in his footsteps, make Notts County number 18 on their long list of scalps, and breathe new life into their reputation as non-league football's ultimate giant-killers.
