articles.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli
articles.summary: The 2. Bundesliga serves up an interesting encounter this weekend as 1. FC Magdeburg welcome FC St. Pauli to the Avnet Arena.The hosts have made an impressiv...
articles.body:
The 2. Bundesliga serves up an interesting encounter this weekend as 1. FC Magdeburg welcome FC St. Pauli to the Avnet Arena.

The hosts have made an impressive start to the campaign, particularly on home soil, and will be looking to strengthen their position in the promotion picture. Meanwhile, St. Pauli arrive in Saxony-Anhalt hoping to bounce back from last weekend's disappointing defeat to Nürnberg and end their remarkable run of away draws.

With both sides having ambitions of challenging towards the top end of the table, Sunday's meeting promises to be an intriguing contest.

Magdeburg head into Sunday's encounter sitting fifth in the standings with 17 points from their opening ten matches, having established themselves as one of the division's most dangerous attacking sides.

Petrik Sander's team were held to a 1-1 draw away to Darmstadt last weekend, with Tobias Müller giving the visitors an early lead before the hosts restored parity.

Although the result prevented Magdeburg from making further ground on the leading sides, their overall performances have been encouraging, particularly at the Avnet Arena.

Indeed, Magdeburg currently boast the joint-best home record in the division, having collected 12 points from their five home fixtures, scoring 15 goals in the process. Four victories from those matches underline the difficulty Sunday's visitors will face.

Their attacking output has also been particularly impressive, with 21 goals scored across their opening ten league matches. Emmanuel Iyoha and Mateusz Żukowski have been especially influential, contributing 11 goals between them.

However, Sander is refusing to underestimate the challenge posed by St. Pauli, despite their recent defeat to Nürnberg.

Speaking ahead of the encounter, the Magdeburg coach described the visitors as a confident team and dismissed the idea that last weekend's performance would necessarily be repeated.

Sander also highlighted St. Pauli's dominance against Nürnberg, suggesting that the 3-1 scoreline did not accurately reflect the balance of play.

Magdeburg will therefore need to be at their best if they are to maintain their impressive home record and continue their push towards the promotion places.

St. Pauli travel to Magdeburg looking to respond after suffering a disappointing 3-1 home defeat to Nürnberg last weekend.

Despite enjoying lengthy spells of possession and creating several promising opportunities, Marcel Rapp's side were ultimately punished for their lack of efficiency in front of goal, conceding twice late in the contest.

The result leaves the Hamburg outfit eighth in the standings with 12 points, having recorded just two victories from their opening ten league matches.

One of the biggest frustrations for Rapp will undoubtedly be his team's inability to turn positive performances into victories. Six of their opening ten league fixtures have ended in draws, while they have scored just 12 goals.

Their away record is particularly unusual, with all five of their away league matches this season ending in draws. While that demonstrates their ability to remain competitive on the road, they will be eager to finally turn one of those results into three points.

Rapp will also be aware that Magdeburg represent a particularly difficult challenge, given their impressive home form and attacking threat.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's fixture, the St. Pauli coach highlighted Magdeburg's individual quality, particularly their willingness to take opponents on in one-on-one situations.

"They are a team that dribbles a lot. That is something special in this league, but we are preparing for it. We have to win a lot of duels," Rapp explained.

The visitors will also be hoping that their attacking players can become more clinical after their frustrating performance against Nürnberg. Abdoulie Ceesay and Branimir Hrgota are expected to carry much of the responsibility in the final third.

A positive result would be particularly valuable for St. Pauli, who could move closer to the promotion contenders with a victory.

St. Pauli have historically enjoyed the better of this fixture, winning six of the first eight meetings between the clubs, with the remaining two ending in draws.

However, Magdeburg finally ended that unwanted record during their most recent encounter in February 2024, recording a memorable 1-0 victory at the Avnet Arena.

Baris Atik scored the decisive goal in the 72nd minute, bringing an end to St. Pauli's remarkable 20-game unbeaten run in the league at the time during their promotion season.

That victory was Magdeburg's first against the Hamburg outfit, and they will be hoping to repeat the achievement on Sunday.

St. Pauli's last victory in this fixture came in February 2023, when they recorded a 2-1 success.

Magdeburg will continue to be without Lubambo Musonda, who remains sidelined with an Achilles tendon rupture. Moritz-Broni Kwarteng is also unavailable for Sunday's encounter.

There is more encouraging news regarding Mateusz Żukowski, however, with the forward expected to be available after recovering from a shoulder contusion which kept him out of the Darmstadt fixture.

Żukowski's potential return would provide a significant boost to Sander's attacking options, particularly given his contribution alongside Iyoha this season.

St. Pauli also still has a few absentees. Rony Jansson has returned to full training after his recent absence, but Rapp confirmed that Sunday's encounter would come too soon for the defender.

Elsewhere, Mathias Pereira Lage and Gisli Thórdarson are also set to miss out.

Otherwise, the St. Pauli coach confirmed that the remainder of his squad were available for selection, providing him with plenty of options as he looks to find the right attacking combination.

Martijn Kaars, a former Magdeburg forward, has also been discussed following his recent struggles in front of goal. Rapp praised his application in training but acknowledged that the striker is currently lacking the goals to match his performances.

1. FC Magdeburg (4-3-3): Reimann; Nadjombe, MacNulty, Müller, Nollenberger; Michel, Hyryläinen, Müsel; Atik, Żukowski, Iyoha

FC St. Pauli (3-4-1-2): Voll; Smith, Nemeth, Ritzka; Pyrka, Fujita, Rasmussen, Oppie; Metcalfe; Ceesay, Hrgota.

articles.title: The Daily Hilario: Open wide for some soccer!
articles.summary: Your daily dose of off-topic shenanigans
articles.body:
Matchweek 10 is upon us in the Premier League — Everton beat Frank Lampard's Coventry City last night, 3-1, to get it started already — and it's the last one for a couple weeks as the international break shall follow after Sunday.

We're one of the last teams to play this weekend, so let's enjoy some other action until then. Enjoy may be in scare quotes.

Today, it's Leeds vs. Spurs in the Who-do-you-dislike-more Derby, then Arsenal vs. Hull City if you believe in miracles, Fulham vs. Newcastle United in a game that sounds entirely unappealing, and then Nottingham Forest vs. Sham City in the nightcap, where we're going to need another miracle.

Only four games in the Premier League today.

There are of course games in other countries, too, because the football never ends.

Of particular interest to probably none of you will be my hometown team going for another win to keep their amazing start to the season going: 11 wins, 2 draws, 0 defeats, sitting eight points clear of always-winners Slovan Bratislava in the one-team league that is the Slovak top division. People are dreaming of a first ever title. But there's a lot of season to go yet…

articles.title: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important”
articles.summary: Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with the club bringing in a number of stars to bolster the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal.One such p...
articles.body:
Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with the club bringing in a number of stars to bolster the squad at Jose Mourinho's disposal.

One such player who arrived with high expectations at the Santiago Bernabeu was Marc Cucurella.

The World Cup winner was expected to be the player who would improve Madrid's squad the most in a position that has been problematic since Marcelo's exit.

Cucurella explains what makes playing for Real Madrid different

Representing Los Blancos has come with expectations that have far exceeded what Marc Cucurella initially anticipated.

The Spaniard has now reflected on the unique responsibility that comes with wearing the Madrid shirt.

"Being a Real Madrid player means that every match against another team is hugely important to them, perhaps the biggest match of the year," the Spanish international explained.

Cucurella has talked about the challenges of playing for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Having spent years at Barcelona coming through La Masia 's ranks, Cucurella understands both perspectives.

"When I used to play against Madrid, that week was special: everyone wanted to come and see you, and they wrote to you," he recalled.

"Ultimately, having the responsibility of winning every match is a wonderful thing and easy to handle."

Facing Real Madrid is always a big occasion for their opponents, but playing for Los Blancos is a whole different challenge.

A responsibility Cucurella is learning to embrace

Cucurella had a difficult start to life at Real Madrid but has come into his own in recent weeks.

Cucurella is embracing his new life in the Spanish capital. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

His performances have coincided with Los Blancos ' upturn in form, and the Spaniard has firmly established himself as Jose Mourinho's first-choice left-back.

Cucurella is also facing significant competition from Alvaro Carreras, who has done nothing wrong in the chances Mourinho has given him.

Between them, the manager has two high-quality options who can start on any given day, and that is a luxury to have.

Cucurella will hope to put in a good performance against Valencia later tonight as Madrid look to extend their winning run to eight games.

It remains to be seen how the Spaniard fares over the course of the season and how the battle between him and Carreras pans out.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel confirms he has picked Real Madrid over Barcelona
articles.summary: Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel has indicated a clear preference for Real Madrid over Barcelona, dealing a blow to the Catalans’ attempts to se...
articles.body:
Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel has indicated a clear preference for Real Madrid over Barcelona, dealing a blow to the Catalans' attempts to secure one of English football's most highly rated young talents.

The recently turned 16-year-old attacker, who has attracted interest from several European clubs, made his position clear during an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca while visiting the Spanish capital.

Asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid, Gabriel did not hesitate, saying: "Barcelona or Real Madrid? Obviously, Real Madrid."

The youngster also revealed his ambitions for the future, making clear that he has his sights set on the highest individual honours in football. "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or," he said.

His comments come amid reports that a move to Real Madrid is progressing , with the transfer close to completion.

Real Madrid move ahead after Barcelona withdraw from transfer race

It is to be remembered that Barcelona had identified the teenager as one of the most exciting prospects available and held several meetings with his representatives through sporting director Deco.

The Catalans attempted to convince the youngster that joining La Masia would offer the ideal environment for his development.

However, the financial demands of the operation also complicated Barcelona's pursuit, with the club eventually withdrawing from the competition.

JJ Gabriel will sign for Real Madrid. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Real Madrid have since moved into a stronger position, even reaching a verbal agreement with Gabriel over a potential move, with the intention of bringing him to the club during the January transfer window.

Barcelona were among a number of suitors, including Bayern Munich and PSG, who held talks with the player's representatives, but the sporting directive offered by Real Madrid made all the difference.

Indeed, it can be argued that Barcelona boasts a better youth academy, but financial considerations also made a big difference.

This is because any move for the 16-year-old would have cost them millions, and it is quite understandable why the Catalan club decided to give up

articles.title: ☀️ ADL-Allegri talks, Bastoni insight and Pavlovic doubt: morning news
articles.summary: Saturday's action gets underway as Serie A matchday 11 continues (after Udinese's defeat, which also saw Zaniolo lose his cool), while abroad, negotiations o...
articles.body:
Saturday's action gets underway as Serie A matchday 11 continues (after Udinese's defeat, which also saw Zaniolo lose his cool ), while abroad, negotiations over youngster JJ Gabriel continue to make headlines.

Here is this morning's biggest news from Serie A's top clubs.

According to Tuttosport , Giovanni Carnevali held up a Juventus scarf during the closing minutes of the Bianconeri's match , which the CEO followed with great emotion.

The scarf was a gift from the Board of Directors after a shareholder at the general meeting urged him to pay attention to the symbolic aspects of his new role as well.

Carnevali was particularly pleased with the gift and is now expected to carry the scarf with him as a good-luck charm.

According to Corriere dello Sport , Pavlovic did not train with the rest of the squad, instead following an individual programme because of the shoulder discomfort that had already forced him to miss the Europa League clash with Ferencvaros.

The Serbian defender therefore remains doubtful for the trip to Genoa : he could play through the pain given the importance of the match, but the final training session will determine whether he can be included in the squad.

Inter: The inside story on Bastoni and Barcelona

According to The Athletic , Barcelona considered signing Alessandro Bastoni in the summer, with sporting director Deco keen on the move, although Flick had some reservations.

In the end, the Catalan club chose to focus on their attack: the coaching staff felt it was essential to sign forwards who could also contribute defensively by pressing high up the pitch. Hence their interest in Anthony Gordon.

Barcelona would also reportedly be willing to sell Alejandro Balde as early as January : his contract enters its final year next summer, and there are no reports of renewal talks. A major sale would allow the Blaugrana to fund potential signings in the winter transfer window.

Napoli: De Laurentiis reassures Allegri and the squad

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , De Laurentiis visited Castel Volturno, where he spent around three hours discussing Napoli's poor run of results with Allegri and Manna.

The president sought to reassure the players before training: "You're good players and good lads too."

There was no ultimatum for Allegri, with De Laurentiis reaffirming his confidence in him : "Stay calm. I'm optimistic, and so are you." The aim is to see a united and determined Napoli as soon as the Lazio game, like the side seen against Roma and Bodo Glimt.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Koné's recovery is the main piece of good news for Gasperini ahead of the match against Sassuolo.

Gollini's absence, meanwhile, should see Devis Vasquez make his first Serie A appearance of the season (after his Champions League debut) . He has not played in the league since May 25, 2025, when he featured in Empoli-Verona.

In defence, Ghilardi and Balerdi are still competing for a starting spot , while Molina is expected to return to the starting line-up on the right flank.

Lazio: Talks over a new deal for Dele-Bashiru

According to Corriere dello Sport , Lazio have reportedly made initial contact with Dele-Bashiru's agents to discuss a possible extension to his contract , which currently expires in June 2028.

The Biancocelesti believe in the Nigerian midfielder's potential, and he could also return to the national team : head coach Eric Chelle has included him in his provisional squad.

Fiorentina: Fan display planned for Juventus clash

According to Repubblica Firenze , Fiorentina are looking to return to winning ways at home against Juventus, ending a drought stretching back to April 13 , when the Viola beat Lazio 1-0.

The Franchi will be sold out for the occasion, with around 24,000 spectators and a display in the Curva Fiesole featuring small flags and funded by the fans themselves.

Vanoli is expected to stick with the line-up used in Reggio Emilia , with Oulai and Gonçalves starting on the bench. Atta and Pongracic will be absent, while Ranieri will try to recover in time.

articles.title: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star
articles.summary: Manchester United have not started the 2026/2027 season in any way, shape or form as they would have imagined in August.SeasonThe Red Devils currently sit 17...
articles.body:
Manchester United have not started the 2026/2027 season in any way, shape or form as they would have imagined in August.

The Red Devils currently sit 17th in the league and have only won one match out of nine.

What's more, they have been dumped out of the League Cup and have won two and lost two of their Champions League matches so far.

United signed Senne Lammens last season from Royal Antwerp and he hugely impressed in the United goal, marking a big step up from Andre Onana or Altay Bayindir.

Nonetheless, this season has been more of a challenge and even though he has not made many big errors, he has conceded too many goals for a United keeper.

Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb have jumped on this possible dissatisfaction with the job Lammens is currently doing and linked the club to Atalanta's Marco Carnesecchi.

The outlet states, "Marco Carnesecchi is on Manchester United's radar."

The site continues, the "Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi has caught Manchester United's eye. The Reds are keen to sign the Nerazzurri player as a backup, partly based on his performances in recent months."

Tuttomercatoweb also claim, "while Senne Lammens was excellent during his first season—even winning awards for his performances—he has now conceded 23 goals in 13 matches, with only one clean sheet to his name so far, against Sabah."

United could even look to do a deal for the Italian as early as January, according to the site.

One potential complexity is that the keeper signed a deal in the spring which keeps him contracted at the club until 2030.

Nonetheless, "a significant contract extension, though one that might not necessarily put an end to the Red Devils' pursuit—even if the fee demanded by Atalanta is far from low."

What's more, "it is clear that the ups and downs of this season in Bergamo could make a potential departure more likely," even if Atalanta have little history in selling their top stars in the winter market.

Carnesecchi has played 15 matches this season in all competitions, conceding 25 goals and keeping three clean sheets.

⚠️ Whilst Lammens has been far from impressive, Carnesecchi's record is hardly better

⚠️ With limited funds and needs in defence and attack, United are unlikely to spend on a goalkeeper in January

We believe that Manchester United have limited funds for January and currently have much greater needs than improving the goalkeeping situation.

Feature image Marco Luzzani via Getty Images

articles.title: What is going wrong for defending champions Larne?
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI explores some of the challenges that Larne are facing so far this campaign after a 4-2 defeat against Cliftonville on Friday night left them nin...
articles.body:
Heartbreak in Europe, an early ToalsBet Senior Shield exit and a nine-point gap to the Irish Premiership leaders - it has been a challenging start to the season for Larne.

Friday's 4-2 defeat by Cliftonville leaves the Inver Reds third in the table with just two wins in their past six games.

For a side that are accustomed to setting the standard in the Irish League's top flight, the early signs of their title defence have been far from convincing.

But what has gone wrong so far this campaign for Gary Haveron's side? BBC Sport NI explores.

One of the biggest questions surrounding Larne before the campaign began was whether they could replace the attacking threat left behind by Andy Ryan's departure.

The 32-year-old netted 70 goals in 121 appearances and was instrumental in their recent Premiership success, as well as their historic European run.

Replacing a player the calibre of Ryan was never going to be easy, but Larne have struggled to find a consistent goalscorer this campaign.

The Inver Reds have scored eight fewer goals than league leaders Coleraine this season, with their summer signings yet to make the desired impact.

Montel Gibson has not scored and has played limited minutes since his arrival, while Kevin O'Hara has netted just once in the league.

Matty Lusty, who scored nine goals last campaign, has shown his ability in spells but his season has been hindered by injuries, while Paul O'Neill is their current top scorer with four goals but he has also struggled to find consistent goalscoring form.

For a side aiming to clinch the Irish Premiership title, having a range of goalscorers will be crucial and Larne are still waiting for key players to find form.

'We need to get back to what makes us, us' - Haveron

Over recent years, Larne's defensive strength has been key to their success.

They conceded just 26 goals last season on their way to the title, but that resilience has been harder to come by this campaign and they have have already let in 14 goals.

Cliftonville were the latest team to expose the chink in Larne's armour, capitalising on mistakes and poor defending from a set-piece for their goals on Friday, with manager Haveron acknowledging it is a worry.

"It's definitely a concern because it's not like us to ship the goals that we're shipping, but we're doing it far too often and frequently," Haveron told BBC Sport NI.

"Listen, they're not bad players and they have not become bad players overnight. We need to get back to what we were doing previously.

"The [European] hangover has well and truly kicked in, and we need to get out of it very, very quickly and get back to what makes us, us. Being resolute and strong defensively and back to winning games of football."

It is not just the number of goals that Larne are conceding which is a concern, but the timings of those goals as well.

At Solitude, Cliftonville netted twice in the opening 10 minutes to gain control and give Larne a mountain to climb.

During the summer, Larne were 10 minutes away from securing a place in the group stages of a European competition for the second time before Lincoln Red Imps produced an impressive comeback to snatch a Uefa Conference League spot.

When Dundela knocked them out of the ToalsBet Senior Shield on penalties, the east Belfast side equalised in the final minute and, in the Irish Premiership, Coleraine netted three second-half goals to come from 2-0 down to win at Inver Park.

Haveron knows the importance of starting and finishing games well, so getting to the bottom of why they are conceding goals so early and late in games will be pertinent to stop the rot.

Larne initially responded well to their European heartbreak and won their next six Irish Premiership matches.

However, their winning run came to an abrupt end against Coleraine and another disappointing defeat by fellow Premiership challengers Linfield soon followed.

The Inver Reds displayed character and fought back in their next match against Bangor, when they came from a goal behind to win 2-1, but they have struggled to build any sustained momentum since.

A frustrating draw against newly promoted Limavady United followed and left them without a win in three home games.

They did end that run with a late 1-0 win against Portadown, but it was far from convincing and after their latest defeat against the Reds, Haveron conceded they face an uphill battle to retain the Gibson Cup.

"It's damaging that you can't drop the points that we've dropped already this season and expect to be in the mix for anything," Haveron continued.

"Listen, we have just got to get back to putting a run together, winning the next game, and try and focus on doing that and hopefully we can build a wee bit of momentum on what we're trying to achieve.

"We need to address it and I need to look at it and I'll not point any fingers at any players without looking at myself, first and foremost."

The colour of the ribbons that were placed on the Gibson Cup only being decided on the final day of last season proves that every season has plenty of twists and turns, so no one will be ruling Larne out of the title race.

There is still plenty of football to be played and the Inver Reds have the quality and experience to put together a run that will have them back into contention.

However, there is little room for error even at this early stage, with an upturn in form much imperative if the side have any ambition of retaining their title.
authors: Jana McCabe - BBC Sport NI journalist

articles.title: 24 ‘pointless races’ in 10 years: Formula 1 has an end-of-season problem
articles.summary: The Sao Paulo GP marks the first of four races to finish the year with the title already wrapped up - it’s not a new issue
articles.body:
Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP's final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year's Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi .

Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective.

Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton 's all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit.

But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers' title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport's ultimate prize on the line.

There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory.

This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness.

Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the "battle for second" or the "best of the rest" tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that.

Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten.

How many races have been left after F1 title clinched?

2026: 4 (Mexico - venue for title clinch)

But, obviously, most of these title races are effectively over long before the final nail in the coffin. This year, we knew Antonelli would not be caught when George Russell's engine let him down (again) in Malaysia. In 2022, Charles Leclerc's crash at Paul-Ricard in July meant there would be no foreseeable route back in the standings.

Sebastian Vettel's comeback from 39 points down with seven races to go in 2012 is an F1 record for the highest points deficit overcome in a title race. Of course, Max Verstappen came mighty close to overturning a 104-point deficit last year, in the end finishing just two points shy of champion Lando Norris. But that is an anomaly.

And here's the thing: F1 continues to publicise record attendance figures – credit should be given here, especially in terms of the surrounding spectacle of entertainment and concerts on offer and ever-increasing capacity capabilities – as well as astonishing global fanbase numbers. Latest stats suggest the number of fans extends beyond 830 million worldwide, 42% of whom are women and 43% are under the age of 35.

Yet in the United States – F1's No 1 target market and a country used to post-season jeopardy with the play-offs after the regular season in NFL, MLB and NBA – this year's move from ESPN to Apple has seen audiences fall. According to a USA Today report in July, six of the nine races to that point saw viewership declines of 13% or greater compared to 2025. Miami and Monaco, strikingly, saw drops of 68% and 66% respectively.

Could this be about a switch from cable to streaming? Or could it be about an underwhelming season on track compared to last year? The answer is probably a bit of both.

In terms of solutions, it is a tricky one. You can point to the American model for sport and keeping eyeballs on the final prize until the end of the season, but you can also point to the Premier League, which has often endured meaningless rounds of matches in May with the title long wrapped up. The counter-argument is that, with top-four, Europa League and relegation battles also at play, there is much more scope for final-day drama.

A comparison, in this respect, is not possible in F1's closed shop. But with 10 sprints on the calendar next year – and three of the final four rounds hosting sprints – perhaps a proper sprint-leaderboard could be created. While obviously superficial, it could give an added competitive edge for the drivers. Similarly, what about an actual qualifying table? It would need actual incentives: perhaps it could result in more prize money? More off-season wind-tunnel time? More margins to gain ahead of the season to follow?

There is no easy remedy. Yet for a sport not afraid to push the boat – whether it be the number of races, sprints or behind-the-scenes camera access – perhaps something new could be floated in order to give the end-of-season countdown an added oomph which, more often than not, it badly lacks.

articles.title: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report
articles.summary: Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that...
articles.body:
Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that have affected the team this season.

According to SPORT , sporting director Deco is examining several possibilities, although the club's limited financial flexibility in January means finding an affordable reinforcement will be a significant challenge.

Barcelona decided against recruiting a central defender during the summer, directing their resources towards strengthening midfield and attack instead.

However, an accumulation of defensive injuries exposed the squad's lack of depth, increasing the urgency to reinforce the position before the second half of the season.

Given Barcelona's financial condition, Deco is exploring loans, affordable transfers and opportunities involving players whose contractual situations could make them accessible.

Fikayo Tomori and Vitor Reis among Barcelona's defensive options

On that note, AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori is one of the leading names under consideration.

The English defender's contract expires in 2027, and Milan are reportedly open to negotiating his departure in January. Interest from several Premier League clubs could nevertheless create competition for his signature.

Barcelona are keeping tabs on Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images)

The Brazilian has struggled for regular opportunities, accumulating just 199 minutes across four appearances this season. A temporary move could offer him valuable playing time, although there is no indication that City are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the season.

Piero Hincapie also attracts Barcelona's attention because of his versatility.

The Ecuadorian can operate at both centre-back and left-back, making him particularly suitable for Flick's defensive requirements.

In fact, Deco has already sounded out his representatives about a potential loan with an option to buy.

Lisandro Martinez and Lucas Beraldo offer different possibilities

His contract situation, experience and ability on the ball make him an interesting candidate, although negotiating with United would not necessarily be easy.

Lucas Beraldo's situation at PSG could result in a January exit. (Photo by Francesco Scaccianoce/Getty Images)

Furthermore, Paris Saint-Germain's Lucas Beraldo has also emerged on the reported shortlist.

The Brazilian's technical qualities and suitability for a possession-oriented defensive system appeal to Barcelona, while his limited involvement under Luis Enrique could potentially create an opportunity.

Jorrel Hato and Jonathan Tah complete the shortlist

Chelsea's Jorrel Hato is another possibility because of his ability to cover both centre-back and left-back.

With competition for defensive places at Stamford Bridge, Barcelona could explore a loan if the Dutchman struggles to secure consistent minutes.

Lastly, Bayern Munich's Jonathan Tah completes the seven-man list.

However, his departure appears particularly difficult because of his importance to the German club, despite Barcelona's interest in his experience and defensive qualities.

articles.standfirst: Koundé, en cambio, sigue al margen
articles.summary: Koundé, en cambio, sigue al margen
articles.body: Christensen y Eric García se ejercitaron con el resto de sus compañeros este sábado, en la última sesión antes de visitar al Atlético de Madrid en el Metropolitano. Ambos futbolistas estaban pendientes de sus sensaciones durante la jornada de hoy para determinar si existían posibilidades de entrar, al menos, en la convocatoria. Y el propio Hansi Flick confirmó tras el entrenamiento que viajarán con el equipo. De este modo, el Barcelona recupera a dos efectivos en la defensa para el cruce de mañana. Eric García sufrió una lesión muscular en el recto anterior del muslo derecho durante el partido contra el PSG, mientras que Christensen cayó lesionado en el encuentro contra el Sevilla, en el que padeció una lesión muscular en el cuádriceps. La situación de Koundé no presenta novedades. Tal y como se esperaba, el defensa francés no participó en el entrenamiento de este sábado y continúa sin poder reincorporarse a la dinámica de grupo. El internacional arrastra un esguince de tobillo desde el encuentro disputado en el Parque de los Príncipes. A su ausencia se suman las de Dani Olmo, Rodri, Xavi Espart y Roony, que también continúan trabajando en su recuperación. Flick volvió a contar este sábado por la mañana con varios jugadores del Barça Atlètic: Hamza, Tunkara, Àlex Campos y Bonfill. Los cuatro se ejercitaron con el primer equipo.

articles.title: Bordalás: “La Conference ya está olvidada”
articles.standfirst: El cuadro azulón visita La Cerámica en busca de sumar los primeros puntos lejos del Coliseum frente a un submarino que llega tras caer goleado frente al PSG
articles.summary: El cuadro azulón visita La Cerámica en busca de sumar los primeros puntos lejos del Coliseum frente a un submarino que llega tras caer goleado frente al PSG
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa con motivo del duelo de este domingo frente al Villarreal. El cuadro azulón visita La Cerámica en busca de sumar los primeros puntos lejos del Coliseum frente a un submarino que llega tras caer goleado frente al PSG. Físicamente: “La Conference está olvidada, estamos centrados en LaLiga, es lo que nos da de comer. Hemos tenido poco tiempo para recuperar y poco tiempo para preparar el partido, no debe ser una excusa. Confío en el compromiso y la responsabilidad de los jugadores”. Zaid: “Confiábamos en que podía estar para el partido de mañana, pero finalmente todavía las sensaciones no eran del todo buenas y no vamos a asumir riesgos, vamos a esperar. Es el último partido antes de este parón, pero está bien, las sensaciones son buenas”. Boselli: “Yo no he hecho nada, ha sido el propio jugador el que ha sido muy comprometido siempre, ha trabajado sin descanso a pesar de jugar poco y siempre ha sumado. Al final ha tenido la oportunidad de jugar y consideramos que lo ha hecho francamente bien. Es la línea que debe seguir, es un jugador que hemos recuperado, me alegro muchísimo por él, sin duda”. Conference: Ya está olvidada la Conference, sabemos que nos enfrentamos a uno de los equipos que mejor crece en España, no a nivel de plantilla, sino a nivel estructural. Es un ejemplo a seguir desde hace años y el potencial de su plantilla es tremendo, presupuesto altísimo, jugadores de nivel altísimo que año tras año pelean por estar en Europa, ahora está jugando Champions. Eso habla de las dificultades del partido de mañana. Los jugadores saben que tienen que hacer un gran partido, confío en el compromiso y la responsabilidad de los chicos. Apercibidos: “Hemos tenido muy poco tiempo de recuperación, analizamos los minutos de los jugadores, el estado de forma del momento para confeccionar el mejor once. No tenemos en cuenta los apercibidos, nos centramos en el partido de mañana, sabemos que tenemos que hacer un gran partido para hacer algo positivo. Sabemos qué es lo que tenemos que hacer para ser un buen equipo”. Afición: “Siempre palabras de agradecimiento, cada partido nuestro deseo es sumar tres puntos, darle una alegría a la afición. El último partido no pudimos darle esa alegría. Nuestra idea es siempre que acabe el partido y se vayan con una alegría y contentos de que el equipo lo ha dado absolutamente todo”. Enes Ünal: “Tenemos jugadores muy cargados de minutos. Enes Ünal venía de un problema que tuvo en el pie, un esguince muy fuerte y arrastra molestias desde entonces, no estaba cómodo, no estaba a gusto. Tenemos que intentar cuidar a los jugadores”. Mercado de invierno: “No hemos hablado de ese tema, estamos centrados en la competición. Ahora tenemos este partido antes del último parón del año. Luego veremos necesidades y posibilidades para poder incorporar o no algún jugador en este mercado próximo. Eso llegará”.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Manchester United forward says 'my dream is to win Ballon d'Or'
articles.summary: Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid.
articles.body:
Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old is still registered at United but has been training on his own in Spain after walking out on the club and relocating with his family.

He has subsequently reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid but no deal has been signed as yet.

On Friday, following one of his sessions, the teenager was approached by Spanish news outlet Marca who presented him with a copy of their newspaper, which featured a front-page story about his expected move to Los Blancos.

The newspaper reported he told them in English: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or."

United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League.

Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport that Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives.

Despite United having Gabriel's registration domestically, it is not thought it could prevent the youngster joining a club overseas as he now has a European Union passport through his mother, who has Cypriot origin.

While Real and United are both in the Uefa Youth League this season, competition rules prevent players from appearing for more than one club in a single season and Gabriel scored a hat-trick in his final appearance for United against Sabah in September.

He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season began.

articles.title: Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona: La Liga – predictions, team news, lineups
articles.summary: Barcelona and Atletico clash on Sunday in a blockbuster encounter which could upend the La Liga title race this season.
articles.body:
Who : Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona What : La Liga, match day 12 Where : Riyadh Air Metropolitano, Madrid, Spain When : Sunday, November 8, at 9pm (20:00 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 17:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

A top-of-the-table clash headlines Sunday’s La Liga action, with Barcelona looking to retain their top spot before the international break as they face challengers Atletico Madrid.

With only two points separating the teams, the blockbuster clash could well be the turning point in the 2026-27 title race should Atletico upset Barcelona.

Diego Simeone’s side have been in terrific form all season and take on Barcelona, bolstered by a seven-game winning streak in the Spanish top flight.

Atletico’s striker Julian Alvarez struggled to find his feet early in the campaign, with a dramatic transfer saga involving Barcelona adding to the uncertainty. But the Argentinian has since rediscovered his form, scoring in each of his last two league outings.

If Atletico have been impressive, Barcelona have been irresistible.

Hansi Flick’s team have netted an incredible 46 goals in just 11 league games; the only team to score more in their first 11 matches of a campaign were Athletic Club in 1930-31 (49).

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal have been the architects of Barca’s lethal attack, with the Brazilian winger leading the goal-scoring charts this season with 15 league goals in 10 games. He is just the second player to reach this tally within 10 games at the start of a campaign after Real Madrid icon Cristiano Ronaldo, who did so in 2014-15 (18 goals in 10 matches).

Ahead of Atletico vs Barcelona, here’s everything to know:

Atletico are second in the La Liga standings, with 28 points from 11 games. They have won nine matches, lost once and drawn as many.

Barcelona lead the La Liga points table with 30 points from 11 games. They have won 10 games and lost only once, suffering a 2-1 Clasico defeat to bitter rivals Real Madrid last month.

Raphinha thriving where Barca envisaged Atletico’s Alvarez

Raphinha is back to his devastating best as Barcelona’s centre-forward, suggesting the Catalan giants have little reason to regret missing out on Atletico’s Alvarez this summer.

The Argentina international tried to force his way out of Atletico to join Spanish champions Barca, whose attempts to engineer a deal angered the Rojiblancos. Barcelona were fined about 600 euros ($675) for their approach for striker Alvarez by the Spanish football federation in October.

Alvarez stayed and later apologised to Atletico fans to try and rebuild bridges, while Barcelona moved on fast, with winger Raphinha developing into an unstoppable force in a previously unfamiliar number nine role.

Raphinha’s form has made the chances of Barca returning for Alvarez next summer remote, and, after penning a new contract until 2030 on Thursday, he will look to underline that against Atletico.

With the Brazilian firing on all cylinders, Flick’s side won 11 games straight across all competitions at the start of the season.

Currently, he has 19 goals in 13 games across all competitions, including a brace each in the last two games.

After joining Barcelona from Leeds United in 2022, the winger grew frustrated under coach Xavi Hernandez, who did not seem to trust him completely.

However, Flick’s arrival and his high-pressing game suited Raphinha to the ground, and the winger has gone from strength to strength, becoming one of the team’s most influential players and one of the captains.

What happened the last time Atletico played Barcelona?

The last time the teams met was in a 2025-26 Champions League knockout game on April 14.

Although Barcelona defeated Atletico 2-1 in Madrid that day, Atletico edged their Catalan opponents 3-2 on aggregate and reached the semifinals.

Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona: Predictions

Opta’s supercomputer gives Barcelona a 49.3 percent chance of winning, while Atletico’s probability of a win stands at 27.5 percent. There is a 23.3 percent chance of a draw.

Atletico have won two of their last five games against Barcelona in all competitions (L3), all of which have taken place in 2026.

The teams faced off twice in the Copa del Rey semifinals in March, with Atleti grabbing a solid first-leg 4-0 win at home before holding on for a 4-3 aggregate triumph, while they also won 2-0 at Camp Nou in the Champions League quarterfinals in April, going through 3-2 on aggregate on that occasion.

In La Liga, though, Barcelona have won in each of their last four trips to the Metropolitano. They are bidding to become just the third team in La Liga history to clinch five straight away wins over Atletico, after Athletic Club in 1955 and Real Madrid in 2013 (both runs of six).

(Last five games in all competitions; latest match first)

Cristian Romero is out with a muscle injury.

Jan Oblak; Marcos Llorente, Marc Pubill, David Hancko, Alejandro Grimaldo; Giuliano Simeone, Obed Vargas, Morten Hjulmand, Alex Baena; Kang-in Lee, Julian Alvarez

Barcelona midfielder Rodri has been ruled out of Sunday’s clash because of a hamstring injury. He was substituted at half-time of Barcelona’s 3-0 Champions League win over Aston Villa on Tuesday.

Spanish media have reported Rodri could miss up to a month.

Jules Kounde (sprained ankle), Xavi Espart (ankle), Dani Olmo (thigh) and Roony Bardghji (knee) are also sidelined with injuries.

articles.title: Villarreal - Getafe | El Villarreal se pone a 1.000: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: Cifra histórica a la que llega de partidos en Primera ante un Getafe que no quiere fiestas
articles.summary: Cifra histórica a la que llega de partidos en Primera ante un Getafe que no quiere fiestas
articles.body: Pocos podían pensar aquel 31 de agosto del año 98 que el partido que el Villarreal iba a disputar en el Santiago Bernabéu como imponente escenario para su debut en la élite, iba a ser el primero de mil. Porque esa es la cifra que confirma que el sueño de Fernando Roig hace tiempo que se convirtió en una gran realidad de nuestro fútbol. Con muchos más éxitos, basados en una gran inversión y una gestión ejemplar, que fracasos. Aquella noche los castellonenses pagaron la novatada para caer por cuatro tantos a uno, pese a que se adelantaron a los tres minutos con un histórico gol de Gica Craioveanu. Estaban por llegar grandes victorias en escenarios como el propio Bernabéu o el Camp Nou, y grandes gestas europeas, imposibles de imaginar por entonces. De esta forma el Villarreal celebra ante el Getafe una cifra histórica que pone en perspectiva sus casi tres décadas de trayectoria en la élite del fútbol español. Y las anteriores efemérides invitarían al optimismo si tuviesen alguna relación directa con lo que va a suceder en el día de hoy. De sus nueve anteriores 'centenarios', el conjunto amarillo se ha impuesto en cinco de ellos, en tres ha empatado y tan sólo ha sufrido una derrota en su partido 400 ante Osasuna. Desgraciadamente para los amarillos la actual situación no invita a excesivas celebraciones ya que se presentan al partido en el peor momento de la temporada. Tras la inesperada derrota ante el Espanyol y la estrepitosa goleada sufrida ante el PSG, las dudas han llegado sobre el proyecto de Iñigo que necesita reafirmar su postura con un resultado positivo y mejores sensaciones ante el Getafe. El regreso de Saliba es la principal noticia para los castellonenses que apostarán por el regreso de Mikautadze y Moleiro al once para buscar un acierto ofensivo que se les está resistiendo a lo largo de toda la campaña y que está lastrando su temporada. El Getafe, por su parte, visita La Cerámica después de una semana en la que los de Bordalás volvieron a ser un equipo reconocible. Tras vencer al Sevilla y competir ante un Brighton que es tercero en la Premier League, en la Conference League, los azulones visitan ahora a un Villarreal en apuros tras la goleada sufrida en Champions frente al PSG. El cuadro del sur de Madrid quiere poner tierra de por medio con el descenso y un triunfo supondría un impulso vital en el objetivo. El equipo azulón aún no sabe lo que es puntuar lejos de su feudo y cuenta todas sus unidades en la tabla por puntos logrados en casa, por lo que el choque contra el conjunto groguet se antoja suculento para poder empezar a sumar como foráneo.

Swansea City centre-back Stephen Welsh has dropped out the Scotland squad for their forthcoming Nations League double-header and been replaced with Los Angeles' Ryan Porteous.

Fears that Welsh had sustained serious knee ligament damage, following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Swansea's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth on Tuesday, appeared to have eased on Thursday.

A scan showed the 26-year-old had not suffered a significant problem and Swansea hoped he could even play some part of their game at Birmingham City on Saturday.

But the Scottish FA has now announced his withdrawal from their matches at home to North Macedonia on Friday and away to Switzerland on Monday, 16 November.

Welsh has earned all four of his caps since Sebastien Pocognoli was appointed Scotland head coach in the summer.

Porteous, 27, last played for Scotland under Steve Clarke in March 2025, coming on as a late substitute to win his 13th cap in a 1-0 Nations League play-off win in Greece.

The former Hibernian defender left Watford for Los Angeles last August, having finished the previous season on loan to Preston, and has made 35 appearances this year for the side sitting sixth in the Western Conference and 12th in the overall Major League Soccer (MLS) table.

Scotland must take at least four points from their final two group games to have a chance of making the promotion play-offs.

articles.title: Portsmouth 1-2 Stoke: Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot score as Potters hit back for victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Portsmouth and Stoke at Fratton Park on Saturday; Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot seal turnaround victory for Mark Robins’ in-form Potters.
articles.body:
Tyrese Shade netted his Portsmouth goal with a lovely bending finish to put the hosts in front, but the Potters turned a tame first half around to make it five away wins in a row.

McGlynn capitalised on goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid's failure to hold on to a cross before Wilmot headed home a rebound.

The match was only two minutes old when referee Ben Speedie paused the action after Stoke wing-back Junior Tchamadeu reported a comment made to him from the stands while he prepared to take a throw-in.

Pompey had scored two stoppage-time goals to beat Swansea at Fratton Park on Tuesday night and almost immediately continued in the same manner.

A short corner routine in the sixth minute appeared to have been wasted when Terry Devlin was closed down on the edge of the area.

But the ball ricocheted off Tchamadeu and into the path of Shade, who had taken the initial corner, and the forward curled a shot past Viktor Johansson for his first Pompey goal.

Stoke offered very little in the first half and an off-target header from Wilmot in the 21st minute was their only attempt before the break.

At the other end, Portsmouth kept the visiting defence on their toes and threatened a second goal.

Centre-back Regan Poole followed a pass from deep and ended up with a shooting opportunity, but the angle was against him and Johansson easily blocked the effort.

Marlon Pack almost picked out the top corner from 30 yards and Odin Bailey's 50-yard run ended up with a stinging drive at Johansson.

Stoke's second shot of the match, their first on target, levelled the scores and sparked the turnaround.

Schmid allowed Ben Johnson's low cross to squirm away from him and Luca Bombino kept the ball in play and squared for McGlynn to thump in.

It was the American's seventh goal involvement in his nine league starts.

Bailey bounced a shot into the ground and over shortly after, but the Potters continued to improve, albeit without testing Schmid again until the 77 minute.

Jack Galbraith had time on the edge of the box to size up a shot and powered it towards the bottom corner.

Schmid saved but pushed the ball back out into the middle of his area, where Wilmot was following up and nodded in his third goal of the season.

Pompey could not create another chance as they faded to bring their six-match unbeaten run to an end.

"I'm really disappointed we lost the game. The contrast in the halves was stark.

"We played very well in the first half and deserved the lead, but we didn't put the game to bed when we could have done.

"The second half was completely different. We started poorly, the details across the team was poor and we got what we deserved.

"We didn't cope with the Stoke equaliser particularly well.

"All of a sudden, the things we were doing with good quality and good detail in the first half, we didn't do in the second.

"Across the board we made too many mistakes. Naturally the goalkeeper will be disappointed, but all the boys should look at themselves and see what we can do better to improve.

"If we had been torn apart by a team that has just gone top of the league and there was nothing we could do, then fine. But that wasn't the case today. Stoke deserved to win in the end, but it was for our undoing."

"That is the first time we have won five on the bounce away from home since 1947. That just shows what an achievement it is.

"The players need to take stock of that and be proud of it. We can go into the international break satisfied and it gives us a lot to be proud of going forward.

"They were on a really good run of form so it doesn't help when you don't start. We weren't us in the first half and we gave them a lead.

"To come back from that and perform like we did in the second half to get the two goals and win was really pleasing.

"At half time I told us to be more us. Second half we were more us and that is one of the most pleasing things from today.

"The connection with the supporters is good at the moment, but we know our end of the bargain. We have to keep it up and keep playing."

articles.title: Bristol City 0-5 Norwich: Canaries thump five past struggling Robins to heap pressure on boss Michael Skubala
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Norwich at Ashton Gate on Saturday; Paris Maghoma, Harry Darling, Andre Brooks, Jovon Makama and a Mathias Kvistgaarden penalty seal a comprehensive Canaries win.
articles.body:
The Canaries took a 22nd-minute lead when Paris Maghoma picked up the ball 40 yards out and ran forward unchallenged before placing a low right-footed shot past Brad Collins from the left side of the box.

It was 2-0 in the 53rd minute, Jason Knight's mistimed header inside his own penalty area directing the ball to Harry Darling who coolly nodded it over Collins' despairing dive.

Three minutes later Maghoma turned provider, pulling a low cross back for Andre Brooks to fire home a third. There were still 20 minutes left when substitute Jovon Makama turned in an Anthony Musaba cross.

Mathias Kvistgaarden added the fifth with an 80th-minute penalty after being pulled down by Lisav Eissat as home fans chanted 'You're getting sacked in the morning' in the direction of Skubala, whose team have already suffered five home league defeats this season.

Bristol City made two changes from the midweek home defeat by Wolves, bringing in Rob Dickie and Adam Randell for Luke McNally and Sam Bell, while the Norwich starting line-up showed one change from the 4-0 rout of Derby, Ben Chrisene replacing Darlin Yongwa.

The visitors had the better of a scrappy first half littered with misplaced passes - particularly by the home side - and notable for only two clear chances.

Norwich grabbed theirs through Maghoma, while the Robins were left to rue a glaring miss by Scott Twine after 31 minutes when the midfielder should have levelled things up.

George Tanner's long throw from the right was headed on into the path of Twine, who contrived to volley straight at Dan Grimshaw from six yards, the goalkeeper saving with a foot when he should have been given no chance.

The Robins left the field to boos from their fans at the half-time whistle, while the large contingent of Norwich supporters who had got up early for the 12.30pm kick-off could reflect on a solid display from their team.

The hosts made a change at the break, sending on Jed Wallace for Cam Pring, and began brightly, Knight heading over from a Rio Cardines corner and then shooting over the crossbar from distance.

At the other end, Jacob Wright saw a curling effort from 25 yards go past the wrong side of a post before two goals in quick succession put Norwich in complete command.

Collins saved well from Wright, while Maghoma and Musaba shot narrowly over as Bristol began to look vulnerable to every attack. Dom Ballard had an effort cleared off the line at the death to complete a nightmare day for his team and Skubala.

Bristol City head coach Michael Skubala:

"The first thing I have to do is apologise to our fans because the second half is not good enough, from me or the players. It was an unacceptable performance.

"It's the first massive blow like that I have had in my career and it really hurts. It's the job of the manager to wear it at times like this and the only thing you can do is work harder.

"Our away form this season has been good and I'm at a loss to explain why we are finding it so hard at home.

"There was nothing in the first half. They scored with their only attempt and we missed a great chance to equalise. That's how it is going at the moment.

"After the second goal we capitulated. I need to look at myself and at the players and we all need to take a look in the mirror.

"We have two weeks now to work hard and look to the future. The international break offers an opportunity to solve some big problems.

"I still believe I can take this club to where we want to be, but this game can hit you in the face really hard and that has happened today."

"We are growing by the week. I am seeing boys becoming men, with clear signs of evolution from so many of our young players.

"That's what we need if we are to get to where we want to be. We want to play attacking football, with goals coming from all over the pitch, not just from our attacking players.

"I am proud of the intensity, the discipline and the quality on the ball we are displaying. The players are hungry and full of desire.

"In all 11 positions we had players making a difference today and when that happens you have a good team.

"We scored five goals and kept a clean sheet, but the best thing of all for me was to see after the game the joy from the whole squad, even those players not involved. That is a big sign that it will be a good season.

"Our supporters are also playing their part. It was a tremendous following for such a long trip and early kick-off today. They stayed behind us when things were not going so well and that is so important."

articles.title: Derby County: How 'calm' Eustace got the result he needed to carry on
articles.summary: How under-pressure John Eustace kept calm to ensure he would carry on as Rams boss by overseeing Friday's come-from-behind win over Bolton.
articles.body:
That was the feeling under-pressure head coach John Eustace had when his Derby County team came into the dressing room at half-time after just going 1-0 down to Bolton Wanderers on Friday night.

While Eustace had previously said he "wasn't surprised" to still to be in charge of Derby for the Championship game after overseeing a 10-match winless run, his tenure was undoubtedly under threat.

And the chance to address his players at the break might have been the last opportunity he would get to trigger a reaction.

Whatever he said certainly worked as two goals in the first four minutes of the second half followed, with 28-year-old Ryan Nyambe netting the first of his career to level before defender Jack Robinson – a hugely experienced player recently recruited to help offset the club's injury crisis – put them 2-1 up with a header.

A third goal from Rhian Brewster in stoppage time completed the much-needed win.

Afterwards, Eustace was quick to highlight that some senior players – including Robinson and latest arrival Shane Duffy - were first to speak up at the interval.

But that's not to say the 46-year-old didn't deliver his own message.

"I certainly let them know my thoughts as well," Eustace told BBC Sport.

"It didn't get heated at all. I believe in the process, I believe in the way I am with the players, sometimes you do get emotional and heated, but not with important stakes like this. If you lose your head and show too much emotion, I don't think it has the right effect.

"We were very calm at half time, the players spoke, we changed our shape and it was about 'right let's go win the second half'."

Derby beat Bolton to ease pressure on Eustace

'The group stuck together & showed spirit'

Boos were last thing Eustace and his players had heard when they headed down the tunnel on the way to the dressing room at the break.

In that moment, having just gone behind to a Ruben Rodrigues goal, the Rams boss admitted they could "quite easily gone under".

Despite Eustace's future at Derby apparently depending on what he did next, he dismissed the notion afterwards that his team talk and half-time tweaks were a last-ditch effort to save his job.

"It certainly wasn't the last throw of the dice, I probably did that one about five or six games ago," he said with a laugh.

"We changed our shape, because it needed to be changed and I felt that we could hurt them on the transitions, and I was quite excited about the second half.

"I was just delighted for the boys really."

While it is the first time in Eustace's 21-month tenure as Derby boss that he finds himself in a position where he needs results to ensure he stays in charge, he likened the feeling he got from the victory against Bolton to those when overseeing the club's miraculous relegation escape when he took charge in the final months of the 2024-25 season.

"Keep calm and carry on" was the mantra that he relied on then as they avoided the drop on the final day – an escape that paved the way for their challenge for a play-off place last season.

When asked about that iconic phrase, which was first used on World War II posters, Eustace said: "That's the way I work.

"This past 15 games has been very challenging, for lots of different reasons, and it was important that I keep believing in what I do and keep believing in the group.

"You can listen to all the outside noise, and listen to what people will do or what I should do, but ultimately I'm in control of the group that I've got. I've been very calm and what will be will be.

"Tonight's performance felt like when I first came in, when we were seven points off, staying up with 11 games to go, and you know we found a way.

"So let's certainly not get carried away, but let's be really proud of the group. It's going to be a long season there's going to be some really difficult times, but when you can perform and fight like we did tonight hopefully that'll be enough to keep moving us in the right direction."

Derby poised for injury boost after break

With two weeks off now for the international break, Eustace also has the added bonus of time that will possibly allow him to call upon some of club's long list of injured players when the campaign resumes.

Prolific US forward Patrick Agyemang has been out with an Achilles tendon injury since April, while defender Matt Clarke, player of the season in 2025-26, has been absent for three months.

"They are two huge players," Eustace said.

"We haven't had them all season and they have certainly been missed, so just to get them back in the group is brilliant."

articles.title: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham: Noah Okafor's winner ends Whites' five-game winless run after Jayden Bogle escapes red card
articles.summary: Report as Leeds deservedly beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road; substitute Noak Okafor strikes late winner; Leeds defender Jayden Bogle escaped a first-half red card for a tackle on Mathys Tel's Achilles; ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean believes Bogle's tackle was "100 per cent a red"
articles.body:
Leeds were deserved victors to earn their first win in six games as Spurs saw their three-game winning run ended - but were left fuming over the Bogle decision.

The Leeds right wing-back caught Mathys Tel on his Achilles, which was awarded a foul but not punished further by referee John Brooks.

A four-minute VAR review then ensued, but Tony Harrington opted against an on-field review, with the challenge only deemed "reckless" as Tel was forced off injured as a result of it.

Ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean believed Bogle's tackle was "100 per cent a red", with the incident coming just a week after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar challenge in Spurs' win over the Eagles.

Leeds took full advantage of the decision, eventually making the breakthrough in the 79th minute through Okafor, who scored just 97 seconds after coming on, combining with fellow substitute Harry Wilson.

Goalkeeper James Trafford denied Jan Paul van Hecke in stoppage time during a rare moment of threat from Spurs, who were described as "poor" by their former captain Michael Dawson on Soccer Saturday .

The victory moves the home side above Spurs into eighth, while Roberto De Zerbi's team drop to 10th, dampening hopes that they may have turned a corner.

De Zerbi was booked in the defeat at Leeds for his frustrations over a second-half caution given to Pedro Porro - a decision he called "incredible" - and will now serve a one-game touchline ban when Spurs return to action after the international break against Ipswich at home on November 21.

Farke: 'Butterfly' Bogle is 'softest player' in PL

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking to TNT Sports on Bogle's red-card escape:

"I didn't watch it back. I just know that Jayden Bogle never, out of any bad intention, does the foul.

"It looked a bit like an unlucky coming together - a very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured right now. Wish him all the best.

"But I know Jadon Bogle - the last thing is that he is a nasty player.

"He's normally probably the softest player in the whole league. I always call him my butterfly. Never out of bad intention, he's there with the foul - that's what I can guarantee.

"But of course, I hope that Mathys can recover pretty quickly."

De Zerbi has 'big confidence' in officials despite Bogle call

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi speaking to TNT Sports on Bogle's red-card escape:

"Pedro Porro was a normal tackle, a normal duel and was an incredible yellow card.

"The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing."

On whether he would have liked an on-field review: "No, I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not.

"There was the VAR, and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence.

"We have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve."

Gerrard: If ref goes to monitor then Bogle is sent off

Ex-England and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard speaking on TNT Sports :

"The contact is dangerous. It is high risk to injure an opponent.

"I think if the referee was told to go to the screen, I think he gives a red card.

"When I first saw it, I just thought it was going to be a yellow card at best, but now that I've seen it so many times and Bogle accidentally - I must say - has potentially caused possible injury to Tel, which tells me that if the referee went to the screen he might have given a different decision on this.

"I believe that referee should've been told to go to the monitor to look at that incident, and it could've had a huge impact on the outcome of this game."

articles.title: Philip Rivers Reportedly Favored Over Russell Wilson for NC State HC Job in New Rumors on Search
articles.summary: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers is reportedly considered the favorite to land the head coaching job at his alma mater of NC State.
articles.body:
Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers is reportedly considered the favorite to land the head coaching job at his alma mater of NC State.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, "all signs are pointing" in the direction of Rivers becoming the next head football coach at NC State despite another former NC State and NFL quarterback in Russell Wilson reportedly also interviewing for the job.

Rivers' St. Michael Catholic High School football team was eliminated from the Alabama state playoffs on Friday night, and Rivers addressed his candidacy at NC State after the game, saying, "We'll see what the future holds."

Per Jones, Rivers "has been assembling his staff the last several weeks" in the event that he is hired.

Talks between Rivers and NC State were first reported by ESPN's Mark Schlabach and Pete Thamel a week ago, and while Wilson emerged as a potential candidate in the days that followed, Jones noted that his entry into the mix "did not materially alter things."

Jones pointed toward the fact that Rivers has much stronger ties in NC State's home of Raleigh than Wilson, partly due to the fact that Rivers' son, quarterback Gunner Rivers, has committed to play at NC State starting next season.

Rivers has no coaching experience beyond the high school level, but he did have a head coaching interview with the NFL's Buffalo Bills this past offseason.

That came on the heels of Rivers temporarily ending a four-year retirement from playing in order to help out the quarterback-needy Indianapolis Colts.

With both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson out injured, the 44-year-old Rivers started three games for the Colts last season, going 0-3, and completing 63.0 percent of his passes for 544 yards, four touchdowns and three interceptions.

It was a valiant effort given how long he had been out of the game, but Rivers hung up his cleats again at the end of the 2026 season in order to refocus on coaching.

Now, Rivers may be on the verge of securing the biggest coaching opportunity of his career with the Wolfpack.

NC State recently fired head coach Dave Doeren after a 3-4 start this season, ending his 14-year tenure in Raleigh.

Doeren went 98-74 and took the Wolfpack to 10 bowl games, but they have not been true contenders for ACC titles, nor have they won double-digit games since going 11-3 in 2002 with Rivers as the quarterback.

articles.title: El extraño penalti anulado en el Málaga-Racing por fuera de juego: los dos jugadores estaban fuera del terreno de juego
articles.standfirst: Díaz de Mera señaló penalti en primera instancia, pero después lo anuló y el VAR confirmó el fuera de juego
articles.summary: Díaz de Mera señaló penalti en primera instancia, pero después lo anuló y el VAR confirmó el fuera de juego
articles.body: El Málaga-Racing dejó una acción poco habitual desde el punto de vista arbitral. Díaz de Mera señaló penalti en primera instancia en el minuto 85 de partido, en una falta de Iker Luque (Racing) sobre Salinas (Málaga). Después, a instancias del juez de línea, lo anuló por fuera de juego. El VAR confirmó la decisión y no hubo penalti. Lo extraño de la jugada fue que tanto Iker Luque como Salinas se encontraban fuera del terreno de juego cuando Joaquín remata cruzado. Que un jugador esté fuera del terreno de juego no significa que no pueda estar en fuera de juego. De hecho, lo normal es estarlo, porque se necesitan dos jugadores por detrás de él para romperlo. En este caso, Salinas sólo tenía a Iker Luque por detrás. Con lo cual, estaba en fuera de juego. Después, Salinas le roba la pelota a Luque y este comete penalti, pero Salinas viene de una posición de fuera de juego. Bien arbitrada la acción, aunque dejara dudas por lo poco habitual que es que un jugador esté fuera del terreno de juego cuando recibe el pase de su compañero. Así explicaba Díaz de Mera la acción tras el partido. "He visto que el defensa derriba y el asistente me comenta que viene en posición de fuera de juego. Hemos mantenido una conversación con el VAR, nos ha confirmado la decisión de fuera de juego y así hemos actuado", señaló en los micrófonos de Movistar LaLiga.

articles.title: Veeyapuram Chundan clinches first win of CBL season at Kainakary
articles.summary: Veeyapuram Chundan wins its first CBL Season 6 race at Kainakary; Melpadom second after time penalty, Aroma third; next race Nov 14 at Kayamkulam.
articles.body: Kottayam: Veeyapuram Chundan, rowed by UBC Kainakary FC, registered its first win of the sixth season of Champions Boat League (CBL) in the ninth race, held at Kainakary on Saturday. CBL is organised by the Keralam tourism department.Racing on its home course on Pamba river, Veeyapuram clocked 3:52.935.Veeyapuram took an early lead of nearly 10 oar lengths in the opening stretch. Aroma Chundan, rowed by Aroma Boat Club, Paravur, Kollam, narrowed the gap to half a boat length by the halfway mark. Aroma had initially finished second but was placed third after the CBL technical committee awarded Melpadom a five-second advantage as Aroma changed its track at the finishing point.Kodikunnil Suresh, MP, inaugurated the races. Members of the CBL governing body, senior tourism department officials and representatives of local self-govt institutions attended. Local competitions for Odi and Veppu boats were also held.After nine races, Aroma retains the top spot in the points table with 82 points.
